text.title: Diary Study Basics Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on behaviour frequency and observability, on whether the study is already in the field, and on whether each entry template can name its trigger moment — separating "do not run a diary study at all" from "specify it here" and "it is already running, go to execution".

decision-tree.root-question: How often does the behaviour occur, and can you already see it without asking?

branch.when: the behaviour occurs less than about twice a week

conclusion.verdict: skip; the window needed to catch two cycles exceeds any realistic incentive budget — use interviews or wait for a denser behaviour

branch.when: the count or timing is already answerable from instrumentation you ship

conclusion.verdict: skip; telemetry beats self-report on counts — reserve the diary for the reasons behind events you can already count

branch.when: the behaviour happens in a single sitting you could sit beside and watch

conclusion.verdict: skip; run contextual inquiry — longitudinal capture adds nothing to a one-session behaviour

branch.when: the behaviour recurs across days or weeks, in moments you cannot be present for
branch.question: Has the study already launched — are participants submitting entries right now?

branch.when: entries are already arriving; recruitment and templates are locked

conclusion.verdict: skip this spec; route to diary-study-execution for compliance windows, event-versus-entry time and coding

branch.when: nothing is fielded yet — the study is still being specified
branch.question: Can every entry template name the moment it fires — a fixed cadence, a scheduled signal, or an event the participant would recognise in their own words?

branch.when: templates are open-ended prompts with no trigger design — 'tell us about your day'

conclusion.verdict: halt before recruiting; classify each template as interval-, signal- or event-contingent and write the named event in the participant's own words

branch.when: triggers are declared, but there is no dedicated capture channel on the participant's own device or no funded incentive

conclusion.verdict: skip until both exist; compliance is bought, not requested, and reminders must land on the same channel the entry is submitted in

branch.when: triggers are declared and both a capture channel and a funded incentive exist

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; entry under three minutes, duration sized to two named behaviour cycles with a novelty window, compliance threshold plus over-recruitment, exit interview anchored to quoted entries
